starting_principles: First Law of Thermodynamics: $dQ = dU + P dV$
Internal energy of an ideal gas (Joule's law): $dU = n C_v dT$
Ideal gas equation of state: $P V = n R T$
Mayer's relation: $C_p - C_v = R$, with adiabatic index $\gamma = C_p / C_v$
assumptions: The working gas is an ideal gas obeying $P V = n R T$.
Heat capacities $C_v$ and $C_p$ are constant over the temperature range.
The process is quasi-static and reversible (frictionless and without shock waves).

ordered_steps.description: Impose the adiabatic condition $dQ = 0$ in the First Law of Thermodynamics.
ordered_steps.operation: Set $dQ = 0$: $0 = dU + P dV \implies dU = -P dV$.

ordered_steps.description: Substitute the internal energy differential for an ideal gas $dU = n C_v dT$.
ordered_steps.operation: Replace $dU$ by $n C_v dT$: $n C_v dT = -P dV$.
assumptions_applied: Ideal gas internal energy depends exclusively on temperature (Joule's law).

ordered_steps.description: Eliminate pressure $P$ using the ideal gas equation of state $P = \frac{n R T}{V}$.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $P = \frac{n R T}{V}$: $n C_v dT = -\left(\frac{n R T}{V}\right) dV$.
assumptions_applied: Ideal gas equation of state $P V = n R T$.

ordered_steps.description: Separate variables $T$ and $V$ by dividing both sides by $n T$.
Express the ratio $R / C_v$ in terms of the adiabatic index $\gamma$.
ordered_steps.operation: Apply Mayer's relation $R = C_p - C_v$ and the definition $\gamma = C_p / C_v$: $\frac{R}{C_v} = \frac{C_p - C_v}{C_v} = \frac{C_p}{C_v} - 1 = \gamma - 1$. Substitute into the differential equation.
Integrate both sides assuming constant $\gamma$: $\int \frac{dT}{T} + (\gamma - 1) \int \frac{dV}{V} = \text{constant} \implies \ln T + (\gamma - 1) \ln V = \text{constant}$.
assumptions_applied: Adiabatic index $\gamma$ is constant over the process temperature range.

ordered_steps.description: Exponentiate both sides to obtain the temperature-volume adiabatic relation.
ordered_steps.operation: Take the exponential of both sides: $T V^{\gamma - 1} = \exp(\text{constant}) = \text{constant}$.

applicability_conditions: Ideal gas with constant adiabatic index $\gamma$.
